::: {#def-causal-model .theorem}
## Causal model

A causal model $\mathcal C$ of an [NPSEM](#def-npsem) $\mathcal M$ under intervention regime $\Gamma$ is the pair of $\mathcal M$ and its [interventional NPSEM](#def-interventional-npsem) $\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}$, with the error terms of the two held equal:

$$
\mathcal{C} = \big(\mathcal{M},\ \mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}\big), \qquad U^{(\Gamma)}_V = U_V \quad \text{for all } V \in \mathbf V.
$$

Here $U_V$ is the error term of $V$ in $\mathcal M$ and $U^{(\Gamma)}_V$ the error term of the corresponding variable in $\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}$.

$\mathcal C$ is an NPSEM describing the behaviour of $[\mathbf V, \mathbf V^{(\Gamma)}]$. The variables $\mathbf V$ associated with $\mathcal M$ are called **observational variables**; the variables $\mathbf V^{(\Gamma)}$ associated with $\mathcal M^{(\Gamma)}$ are called **counterfactual variables**, obtained by recursive substitution. A counterfactual under the static regime that sets $V$'s parents to the values $\mathbf{pa}_V$ is written $V^{(\mathbf{pa}_V)}$.
:::
